Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Self-reported sadness/depression was less prevalent in vitamin D sufficient adolescents than in insufficient or deficient ones.
Sentence: "The prevalence of self-reported anger, anxiety, poor quality sleep, sadness/depression, and worry was significantly lower (P < 0.05) in vitamin D sufficient participants compared with their other counterparts."
Measured as: self-reported sadness/depression
Population: 1095 Iranian school students, mean age 14.7 years
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D status (sufficient vs insufficient vs deficient), observational
Comparator: Vitamin D insufficient and deficient groups
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,095
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Study B tests vitamin C supplementation rather than vitamin D, making the pair off-question.",
  "verdict": "off_question",
